s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and evolving left ventricular dysfunction
salient_findings: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
Inducible angina at 50 W without ECG changes
Significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis with in-stent restenosis
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
New QTc prolongation to 500 ms and severely reduced LVEF of 35%
key_facts: 67-year-old man
Hypertension
Dyslipidaemia
Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
Active smoking (35 pack-years)
Family history of ischaemic heart disease
Prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Recent exercise stress test induced angina
Normal sinus rhythm on admission
Q waves in lead III and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF on ECG
Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities on initial echocardiography
Patent stents in the circumflex artery and non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiography
Significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis with in-stent restenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 after transfer to the intensive care unit
Subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch on second angiogram
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation requiring external shocks and cardiopulmonary resuscitation
New QTc prolongation to 500 ms and severely reduced LVEF of 35% on post-resuscitation ECG and echocardiography

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Evolving left ventricular dysfunction with akinesia of apical segments and severely reduced LVEF

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis

shortlist.label: Stent thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: In-stent restenosis and subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: New QTc prolongation to 500 ms on post-resuscitation ECG

shortlist.label: Vasospastic angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent chest pain and coronary artery spasm suggested by subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, new QTc prolongation, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% after an intense emotional and physical stressor, along with the characteristic echocardiographic findings of akinesia of all apical segments and hyperkinesia of the basal segments, is most consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The patient had patent stents and no significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and the echocardiography showed no regional wall-motion abnormalities initially

rejected.label: Stent thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient's stents were patent on the second angiogram, and the subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch was successfully treated with balloon angioplasty

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's QTc prolongation was a new finding after the cardiac event, and there is no mention of a family history of Long QT syndrome or previous episodes of torsades de pointes

rejected.label: Vasospastic angina
rejected.why: The patient's presentation with ST-segment elevation and ventricular arrhythmias is not typical of vasospastic angina, and the coronary angiography did not show significant vasospasm
